item.title: Children need more free time as school pressures take toll, Commissioner’s report finds
item.description: The Commissioner for Children’s annual child participation report found academic pressure was the leading systemic source of stress for children, with bullying, competition over performance and worries about artificial intelligence also cited. It recommends that a minimum amount of daily free time be enshrined in the national curriculum to curb excessive workloads, and that mental health literacy and critical thinking be embedded in teaching. The Commissioner separately launched initiatives for World Children’s Day on 20 November, themed “My Day, My Rights, My Future”.

The Commissioner separately launched initiatives for World Children’s Day on 20 November, themed “My Day, My Rights, My Future”.

Sources: Times of Malta

item.title: Bedingfield calls for Mediterranean EU ministers to meet on defence and security
item.description: Home Affairs and Security Minister Glenn Bedingfield proposed that ministers from nine Mediterranean and Southern EU states meet to discuss defence and security, arguing peace and stability in Europe cannot be achieved without the same in the Mediterranean. He made the call at the first EU-MED Peace and Security Forum in Brussels, urging Europe to “act early rather than wait for problems to become crises”. He linked regional instability in Libya and Syria directly to Malta’s sea routes, energy supplies and economic security.

item.title: Family doctors urge tougher national conditions on tobacco smoking and vaping
item.description: The Malta College of Family Doctors and the Association of Private Family Doctors have urged the government to impose “tougher conditions” on smoking and vaping, noting Malta is the only EU member state holding out against the bloc’s Tobacco Taxation Directive. They said tobacco is behind a substantial share of cardiovascular, respiratory and cancer cases, which account for almost half of Malta’s annual mortality toll. Suggested measures include wider access to cessation medication and classes, more staff training in motivational interviewing, and more smoke-free areas.

item.title: Mixed movements across 13 Malta equities as index stays flat
item.description: The Malta Stock Exchange equity index was practically unchanged at 4,312.8 points, with gains in HSBC, PG, APS, Bank of Valletta and Computime offsetting declines in BMIT Technologies, International Hotel Investments and Malita Investments. Total trading value in local equities was €0.22 million, and APS Bank closed at its highest level since February 2025. The RF MGS bond index slipped 0.12% as euro-area inflation accelerated to 4.0% in October.

item.title: Safe city concept to be extended to Marsa, with Ħamrun, Sliema and Valletta to follow
item.description: Security Minister Glenn Bedingfield said the “safe city” concept is being extended to Marsa, following San Ġiljan, Is-Swieqi and Buġibba, with Ħamrun, Tas-Sliema and il-Belt to work on the plan in the coming days. He said the crime rate per 1,000 people fell from 46 in 2005 to 27 in 2025, while warning that cybercrime is rising as burglaries fall. More CCTV cameras are being added in problem areas, and resident associations were praised for helping police spot suspicious activity.

item.title: MAM suspends industrial action over trainee appointment delays
item.description: The Medical Association of Malta has suspended the industrial action due to start on Friday after “progress” on trainee appointments, saying basic specialist training and GP trainee applicants will begin training on Monday. The association insisted outstanding appointments must still be processed urgently and that the formal trade dispute remains open until lasting measures are agreed. It said the six-month recruitment delay, from the May call to a November 23 start date, exposed underlying problems in the system.

item.title: Suspected fuel smuggler fighting extradition to Spain granted bail
item.description: Maltese businessman Rodrick Grech has been granted bail after being charged over his alleged involvement in a network suspected of laundering €153 million between 2021 and 2024. He was arrested at his company’s premises in Santa Venera after Spain issued a European Arrest Warrant, and he does not consent to being surrendered. Investigators allege the network used a Bulgarian-registered company and 14 other shell companies in Spain to source petroleum products while evading VAT.

item.title: Speaker Carmelo Abela begins school visits to bring Parliament closer to youths
item.description: Speaker of the House Carmelo Abela has started a series of visits to schools, beginning at St Albert the Great College in Valletta where he met students and discussed the work of Parliament. The initiative, prompted by the college rector, is aimed at bringing Parliament closer to the public and particularly to children and young people. He also met primary and secondary pupils who had prepared questions about the role of the Speaker and Parliament.

item.title: European Commission tells Malta to stop finch trapping, rejects ‘research’ justification
item.description: The European Commission has sent Malta a reasoned opinion saying the country’s finch-trapping derogation “does not pursue a genuine research purpose” and that Malta is not complying with the EU Birds Directive. Malta has two months to respond before the dispute can be referred to the Court of Justice. The Commission called on Malta to “stop authorising finch trapping”, adding that enforcement and alternative solutions remain inadequate.

item.title: db Group to cover new €400 infrastructure and driving licence charges for non-EU workers
item.description: db Group has said it will cover the new €400 annual infrastructure contribution and €83 monthly driving licence charge introduced in Budget 2027 for its non-EU workers. The hotel, hospitality and real estate group behind the Hard Rock Hotel announced the move on LinkedIn as part of a “financial support package” in response to the budget measures. The measures have drawn criticism from unions and opposition parties, and further employer responses are expected.

item.title: Man acquitted of drug-trafficking charge after 26-year case
item.description: A 54-year-old man was acquitted of a drug-trafficking charge after a case that ran for more than 26 years. Joseph Camilleri was arrested in July 2000 during a police raid on his Żurrieq apartment and two family-linked residences, where officers said they found heroin, cannabis, cocaine and about 82 grams in capsules. He was later convicted only of possession of those drugs.

item.title: Man fined €1,400 and placed on probation for threatening Floriana mayor
item.description: Rittmar Hatherly, 38, whose criminal record the court described as being of “biblical proportions”, was placed on a three-year probation order and fined €1,400 after admitting to nine charges arising from a September incident in Triq San Publiju, Floriana. The charges included insulting, threatening and offending the mayor, disturbing public order, public drunkenness and breaching bail conditions. He was also ordered to stay away from the mayor for six months.

item.title: Approved new dwellings down 37.4% year on year
item.description: National Statistics Office figures show approvals for new homes fell 37.4% in the third quarter of 2026 compared with the same period in 2025, to 2,298 dwellings from around 3,671. Building permits issued declined 25.1% to 444, averaging 5.2 dwellings per permit, with apartments accounting for the bulk of approvals. The drop is set against sustained debate over Malta’s housing supply and population growth.

item.title: €50 million St George’s Mall shopping centre inaugurated in St Julian’s
item.description: A new €50 million shopping mall with 60 retail and catering outlets was inaugurated in St Julian’s by Prime Minister Robert Abela. St George’s Mall forms part of db Group’s development on the former Institute of Tourism Studies site and spans 15,000 square metres over two floors, with 18 food and beverage outlets and a mix of international fashion brands, shops and restaurants.

item.title: Health warning over excessive chlorate levels in baby food batch
item.description: Health authorities have warned that a batch of Prime Pappe puréed baby food made from salmon and vegetables contains excessive chlorate levels and must not be consumed. The affected lots are 21201649 and 68218990, with a best-before date of 06/11/2027, and consumers are advised to dispose of the product or return it to the store. Chlorate can damage red blood cells and kidneys and interfere with thyroid hormone production, which is a concern for babies and young children.

item.title: 26 residents’ groups slam authorities over failure to tackle entertainment noise
item.description: A coalition of 26 residents’ associations and NGOs, representing communities in 24 localities including Flimkien għal Ambjent Aħjar and Il-Kollettiv, expressed serious concern over excessive noise from entertainment establishments. The groups accused the authorities of failing to enforce regulations and of confusion over which rules apply, worsening the burden on residents. Their intervention adds to the long-running debate over licensing, monitoring and music noise enforcement in Malta.

item.title: db Group’s SD Finance issues €10 million five-year bond
item.description: SD Finance plc, the financing arm of db Group, has announced a €10 million bond issue maturing in five years. It is the first under a bond programme of up to €40 million, guaranteed by db Group subsidiary SD Holdings Limited and approved by the Malta Financial Services Authority. The company plans to list the bonds on the stock exchange, with proceeds going towards refinancing an earlier €65 million bond issue.

item.title: Water main bursts on Marsa’s main road after contractor strikes pipe
item.description: A Water Services Corporation main pipe burst on Triq Aldo Moro in Marsa on Friday morning after a third-party contractor damaged it during works, sending water into the air and leaving part of the busy artery wet. The corporation said no area will have its water supply disrupted because of network redundancies, and crews were dispatched to carry out repairs. Motorists passing through the area, one of Malta’s main traffic corridors, faced slowdowns.

item.title: Momentum urges Malta to move from reacting to preventing domestic violence
item.description: Momentum said Malta must shift from reacting to domestic violence incidents towards actively preventing abuse, identifying warning signs early and giving victims timely protection. Recommendations from a party gathering of experts, educators, social care professionals and activists include faster court proceedings, better coordination between criminal and family courts, stronger institutional accountability and sustainable funding for support organisations. Participants also highlighted lengthy reporting procedures, financial dependence and stigma as persistent gaps.

item.title: Woman jailed three years for defrauding elderly victim of €15,000
item.description: Tania Borg, 36, from Marsa, was sentenced to three years in prison after being found guilty of defrauding an 80-year-old woman of €15,000 through a supposed investment in a detergent business promising returns of about 10%. She was also convicted of misappropriation, breaching two bail decrees and recidivism, but acquitted of forgery charges. The case dates to October 2018 and was reported to police in March 2019.

item.title: 73% of small businesses say Malta is heading in the wrong direction as labour shortages persist
item.description: The Malta Chamber of SMEs’ Q3 Barometer found that 73% of small and medium-sized firms believe Malta is moving in the wrong direction, up nine percentage points from 64% a quarter earlier. Employee shortages remain the leading challenge, cited by 38.3% of respondents, with inflation, traffic congestion, quality of life, good governance and planning also weighing on businesses. The survey drew 397 responses between 12 and 23 October and was published with MISCO, before the Budget 2027 speech. Separately, only 19% of SMEs expect the next 12 months to be a good time to invest.

item.title: Caruana says 2018 population report warning on growth will finally be published
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana said he will publish the 300-page population report he drafted in 2018 after receiving permission to do so, having warned his own government about fast population growth since 2017. The report was previously shelved and its delayed release has fed a long-running dispute over Malta’s population figures. Caruana said publication will come “in the coming days”, while the prime minister has given no firm commitment on the document.

item.title: New loading bays in Birgu raise residents’ questions over authorisation
item.description: Residents in Birgu have raised concerns over three on-street parking bays in Triq Sant Anton that became unloading bays overnight, saying the designation appears to lack Transport Malta authorisation and may be reserved for particular individuals or businesses. Birgu mayor John Boxall said the bays were discussed and approved at council level to help the commercial community, and confirmed CCTV cameras were installed at LESA’s request. Residents also complain that LESA fines have been issued for brief use of the bays while loading belongings.
